description:
Welcome to the team where caffeine is our fuel and deadlines are our natural habitat.
We’re a bunch of curious builders who like turning random ideas into questionable prototypes that somehow work. We’re interested in AI, engineering, coding, problem-solving, and creating things that make people say, “Wait… you actually built that?”
We’re looking for teammates who are creative, willing to experiment, communicate well.
summary:
PLANETARY LAB is a planetary exploration decision-support tool that identifies Earth locations resembling lunar and Martian environments and evaluates how rover designs perform on those terrains.

We developed three integrated components: a 3D rover simulator using NASA’s Perseverance as its reference, a terrain and analogue analysis engine, and JARVIS, a text-based engineering assistant. The platform processes elevation data to calculate terrain slope, roughness and classifications, compares environmental characteristics, and simulates rover performance, including traction, wheel slip, soil sinkage, energy consumption, temperature and radiation exposure. Users can also upload their own elevation data and modify rover parameters to test engineering improvements.

PLANETARY LAB addresses the challenge by helping identify and evaluate terrestrial analogue sites through transparent, data-driven comparisons. It matters because better simulations and analogue selection can improve planetary mission preparation while reducing testing risks and costs.
details:
PLANETARY LAB is a planetary terrain analogue and rover decision-support platform designed to help answer two questions: Where on Earth can we find terrain resembling the Moon or Mars, and how would a rover perform on those environments?

The project integrates three components:

1. Terrain and Analogue Intelligence Engine

The engine processes digital elevation data to calculate terrain characteristics such as slope, roughness and terrain classifications. It compares Earth locations with lunar or Martian reference characteristics and generates a similarity assessment alongside data coverage. Users can also upload their own GeoTIFF elevation files to analyse additional locations. Missing measurements are treated as unavailable rather than assumed to be zero, helping maintain transparency in the results.

2. Rover Simulation Environment

The simulator uses NASA's Perseverance rover as its engineering reference. Users can modify rover parameters and compare different configurations on identical terrain. It explores important mobility and engineering factors, including slope climbing, traction, wheel slip, soil sinkage, power and energy consumption, temperature and radiation exposure. Its calculations draw on established engineering concepts, including the Bekker pressure-sinkage model, Janosi–Hanamoto shear model and Mohr–Coulomb soil-strength relationship. A 3D environment also represents terrain features such as craters, rocks and boulder fields.

3. JARVIS Engineering Assistant

JARVIS is a text-based assistant that helps users understand simulation results and calculations. It operates in an assist-only mode, using calculations already available in the application rather than independently controlling the rover.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Selecting suitable terrestrial analogue environments can help researchers investigate planetary surface conditions and prepare for rover testing. PLANETARY LAB brings terrain analysis and rover engineering simulation into one workflow, allowing users to explore potential analogue locations, test design modifications and understand engineering trade-offs before considering physical testing.

Its intended impact is to make planetary exploration concepts more accessible to students, researchers and engineering enthusiasts while supporting more informed early-stage mission planning.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of PLANETARY LAB is its integration of two normally separate investigations: planetary terrain comparison and rover mobility simulation. Instead of simply identifying a location that looks similar to another planet, the platform also explores how a rover might behave on that terrain. Users can change engineering parameters and investigate how those changes affect performance.

Tools and Technologies

The project uses a browser-based application (index.html) and a Python package for terrain and analytical processing. Its technologies include HTML, JavaScript, Python, Three.js for 3D visualisation and geotiff.js for elevation-data processing. It also uses open geospatial datasets and published planetary mission information.

Factors Considered

The project considers terrain similarity, data availability, rover mass, wheel characteristics, soil behaviour, slope, energy requirements, temperature and radiation. It also distinguishes published reference values, derived calculations and scenario assumptions.

PLANETARY LAB is an early-stage decision-support prototype, not a mission-certified simulator. Earth terrain cannot fully reproduce lunar or Martian gravity, atmosphere or radiation conditions. Some soil, obstacle and environmental parameters are simplified assumptions, and these limitations are disclosed so that results are interpreted responsibly.
dataRefs: NASA's Planetary Geology, Geophysics and Geochemistry Laboratory
